answer: An agent market requires every identity to lock a refundable bond before bidding for work, whether it trades willow cuttings, tracks raven populations, or sells velvet. The bond stays locked for 30 days after each job, so an attacker cannot recycle one deposit across thousands of active identities. Creating 1,000 agents requires 1,000 bonds, tying up capital for the full lock period and making a swarm costly to maintain.
